_comment: Shared OCR line-split cases, read by internal/ocr (splitWideGaps) and extension/src/ocr-cluster.js (splitWideGaps). The stitch cases are the word boxes the desktop engine actually returned for the two touching speech balloons of a public-service Superman page (ticket 67): the balloons' rows are stitched into one recognizer line and the touching outlines are read as tokens of that line, so no gap between words holds the boundary stroke - it runs inside the boundary token's box. A word box taller than the type-size ratio (1.6) x the line's median word height reaches into a neighbouring row, which no lettering of one line does, so the split cuts before it. The single-line case is the guard: a real line of one size is never cut.

cases.name: row one: outlines read as a tall token between the balloons
row two: a lone tall token where the outlines touch
want: A J] ON LUCK! I MAY

cases.name: one real line of one size is never cut
